tasks.short: Draw sketches and floor plans of displays

steps.what: Open the brief for the proposed display
Prepare floor plans and sketches of displays
Keep the model that matches the brief

tasks.design: The brief is opened from {DOCS}. Preparing sketches, floor plans, or models of proposed displays stays with the displayer. Nothing is generated, and a brief is not a sketch.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sketches were loose sheets with no link to the brief.
tasks.enabler_now: The brief can be open while the sketch is made.
tasks.still_hard: The drawing and the model are the displayer's hand.
tasks.human_edge: The displayer knows a proportion that looks wrong only when drawn.
tasks.altitude: The brief is open. The sketch is still drawn by the displayer.

evidence.claim: A brief is a record. It does not draw. The source pack says a locked template can be filled from a table and a person checks it, and that the final selection of a design stays manual.

The source pack says a generated image must be marked, and that naming faces in an archive is biometric data needing explicit consent. This work does not generate the display and does not name faces. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a display is proposed and ends when the displayer keeps the sketch.
A brief has a display id and the constraints, produced by the store. The sketch is made by the displayer. The screen does not generate it.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the displayer's effort.
A missing sketch, price, or plan is not invented. The displayer does that part by hand.
The incremental hour updates the list when the source row changes.
unknowns: Whether proposals are given an id before they are drawn.
research_questions: Who keeps the sketch that will be built?

already_counted.description: The hands-on time is already in the main step.

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when the brief is spoken. The sketch stays the displayer's. No image is generated. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Instruct sales staff in color coordination

steps.what: Open the rack plan and the color list
Instruct sales staff in color coordination
Note counter displays that were not covered

tasks.design: The rack plan and the color list are opened from {DOCS}. Instructing sales staff in color coordination of clothing racks or counter displays stays in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Color rules were a verbal habit that new staff did not hear.
tasks.enabler_now: The color list for the racks can be opened.
tasks.human_edge: The displayer sees a garment the list calls one color and the light another.
tasks.altitude: The list is open. The instruction stays at the rack.

reach.task: Keep the coordination on the rack

evidence.claim: A color list is configuration. The source pack says a locked template can be filled from a table and a person checks it, and that the final selection of a design stays manual.

The source pack says a generated image must be marked, and that naming faces in an archive is biometric data needing explicit consent. This work does not generate the display and does not name faces. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when racks are to be coordinated and ends when the instruction is given.
A rack has an id and allowed colors, produced by the plan. A color not on the list is not treated as specified.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the displayer's effort.
A missing sketch, price, or plan is not invented. The displayer does that part by hand.
The incremental hour updates the list when the source row changes.
unknowns: Whether color rules are written per rack.
research_questions: Who else instructs sales staff when the displayer is not there?

already_counted.description: The hands-on time is already in the main step.

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when colors are not listed. Instruction stays in person. The range is below that case.

steps.what: Open the decoration list for the building
Install decorations and banners on the building
Note bunting the fixings could not take

tasks.design: The list of flags, banners, festive lights, or bunting is opened from {DOCS}. Installing them on the building, street, exhibit hall, or booth stays physical.
tasks.previous_blocker: Decoration lists were a van load with no order.
tasks.enabler_now: The list can name what is to be installed and where.
tasks.still_hard: Installation is physical, and the fixing may not hold.
tasks.human_edge: The displayer sees a fixing the list treats as sound.
tasks.altitude: The list is in order. Installation stays in the hands.

evidence.claim: A decoration list is configuration. The source pack says a locked template can be filled from a table and a person checks it, and that the final selection of a design stays manual.

The source pack says a generated image must be marked, and that naming faces in an archive is biometric data needing explicit consent. This work does not generate the display and does not name faces. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when decorations are to be installed and ends when they are installed.
A decoration has an id and a place, produced by the event plan. A place that is not on the list is not treated as required.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the displayer's effort.
A missing sketch, price, or plan is not invented. The displayer does that part by hand.
The incremental hour updates the list when the source row changes.
unknowns: Whether the list names the building, street, hall, or booth.
research_questions: Who accepts a decoration that could not be fixed as drawn?

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when the list is a van load. Installation stays physical. The range is below that case.

tasks.short: Cut designs to the event motif

steps.what: Open the motif for cardboard designs
Cut designs on cardboard for the event
Note plywood the motif did not fit

tasks.design: The motif is opened from {DOCS}. Cutting designs on cardboard, hardboard, or plywood stays in the hands, according to that motif. The motif is not a cut piece.
tasks.previous_blocker: Motifs were a sketch that got lost among offcuts.
tasks.enabler_now: The motif can stay open while the piece is cut.
tasks.still_hard: Cutting is physical, and the board may not match.
tasks.human_edge: The displayer feels a cut the motif draws as a single line.
tasks.altitude: The motif is visible. The cut stays in the hands.

reach.learn: Which board did not fit the motif

evidence.claim: Opening a motif is configuration. The source pack says a locked template can be filled from a table and a person checks it, and that the final selection of a design stays manual.

The source pack says a generated image must be marked, and that naming faces in an archive is biometric data needing explicit consent. This work does not generate the display and does not name faces. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a motif is issued and ends when the design is cut.
A motif has an event id and a drawing, produced by the designer. A board that is not named is not assumed.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the displayer's effort.
A missing sketch, price, or plan is not invented. The displayer does that part by hand.
The incremental hour updates the list when the source row changes.
unknowns: Whether motifs name cardboard, hardboard, or plywood.
research_questions: Who accepts a cut that departs from the motif?

already_counted.description: The hands-on time is already in the main step.

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Saving falls when the motif is a loose sketch. Cutting stays physical. The range is below that case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Sketches are drawn by the displayer. Instruction of sales staff stays in person. Decorations are installed. Designs are cut by hand to the motif.
reach: Sales staff hear the color rule from the displayer.
A cut that does not fit the motif is noted.
skills_to_grow: Do not treat a decoration list as already hung.
role.ambitious_version: The motif is open before the cut, and the cardboard is still cut by hand.
